title: Chapter 5: The Rescue of the Tin Woodman
chineseTitle: 第 5 章：拯救铁皮木夫

paragraphs.en: When Dorothy awoke the sun was shining through the trees and Toto was out chasing birds around them. She sat up and looked about her, and there was the Scarecrow, still standing patiently in his corner, waiting for her. 'We must go and search for water,' she said to him. 'What do you want water for?' he asked. 'To wash my face after the dust of the road, and to drink, so the dry bread will not stick in my throat.'
paragraphs.zh: 当多萝茜醒来时太阳正穿透树木照耀着，托托在外面在他们周围追逐着鸟儿。她坐了起来环顾四周，稻草人还在那里，依然耐心地站在他的角落里等待着她。“我们必须去寻找水，”她对他说。“你想要水干什么？”他问。“为了在路的尘土后洗脸，以及喝水，以便干面包不会卡在我的喉咙里。”

paragraphs.en: They walked into the forest and soon heard a rusted groan. Investigating the sound, they discovered a man made entirely of tin, holding an axe raised in the air, frozen completely stiff! 'Oil-can! Oil-can!' rusted the Tin Woodman through his stiff jaws.
paragraphs.zh: 他们步入森林，很快听到了生锈的呻吟声。调查这个声音，他们发现了一个完全由铁皮做成的人，手里举着一把斧头僵硬冻结着！“油罐！油罐！”铁皮木夫穿过他僵硬的双颚生锈地呼喊。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy quickly fetched an oil-can from his cottage and oiled his joints until he could move freely. The Tin Woodman explained that an enchanted axe had severed his limbs, and he had lost his heart when he was replaced piece by piece with tin. 'I want to ask Oz for a heart,' he said, 'for love is the greatest thing in the world.'
paragraphs.zh: 多萝茜迅速从他的农舍拿来一个油罐，给他的关节抹油直到他能自由移动。铁皮木夫解释说一把被施了魔法的斧头砍断了他的四肢，当他被铁皮一块接一块地替换时他失去了他的心。“我想向奥兹要一颗心，”他说，“因为爱是全宇宙中最伟大的东西。”

paragraphs.en: The Yellow Brick Road wound onward through the magical countryside of Oz, flanked by sparkling brooks, colorful wild flowers, and strange golden trees. Dorothy tightly held Toto in her arms, her magical Silver Shoes sparkling with every step she took toward their goal.
paragraphs.zh: 黄砖路沿着奥兹国奇幻的乡村继续盘旋，两侧环绕着闪烁的小溪、绚丽的野花与神奇的金树。多萝茜把托托紧抱在怀里，她魔法银鞋在她朝目标迈出的每一步中都闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: 'No matter how dreary our home in Kansas may be,' Dorothy remarked softly to the Scarecrow, 'we people of flesh and blood would rather live there than in any other country, be it ever so beautiful. There is no place like home.'
paragraphs.zh: '无论我们在堪萨斯的家多么沉闷，'多萝茜对稻草人软软地注意到，'我们血肉之躯的人们宁愿住在那里，也不愿住在任何其他国家（无论它多么美丽）。没有任何地方像家一样。'
